stories: story-026 (migrateOne self-call + dust skip + skipCurrent, audit-08 M-02)

noUnboundedLoops.evidence: Two loops. seedUsers :149-151 is bounded by the owner-supplied calldata array (owner-controlled, not attacker-controlled). migrate :188-212 is bounded by caller-supplied maxIterations and clamped to users.length at :185-186.

coreInvariants.name: The cursor always advances
coreInvariants.statement: A migrate call with maxIterations > 0 cannot leave migrateIterator unchanged due to a reverting user position
coreInvariants.evidence: Every per-user outcome in the loop :188-212 advances `i`: zero position -> continue (:193); dust below minStake -> event + continue (:194-200); otherwise the ENTIRE per-user body runs inside `try this.migrateOne(...)` (:202) whose catch (:204-211) merely emits UserMigrationSkipped and falls through. The cursor is committed at :214-218. This is the audit-08 M-02 fix.
coreInvariants.caveat: Scope-limited by design and documented at :71-77: try/catch absorbs REVERTS, not gas exhaustion — under the 63/64 rule an OOG migrateOne can starve the rest of the pass. skipCurrent (:284) is the owner backstop.

coreInvariants.name: migrateOne must NOT be nonReentrant
coreInvariants.statement: Adding nonReentrant to migrateOne would silently skip EVERY user
coreInvariants.evidence: migrate holds the OZ v5 ReentrancyGuard lock (:172 nonReentrant) when it self-calls migrateOne (:202). OZ v5's guard is a single lock shared across all guarded functions, so a guarded migrateOne would revert ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall — and the catch at :204 would swallow it as a per-user skip, producing a silently no-op pass. The contract instead gates with `require(msg.sender == address(this), "Only self")` (:236). Rationale documented at :227-234. RECORDED AS A REGRESSION TRAP: any future 'hardening' that adds nonReentrant here is a silent, total failure that still emits a clean-looking completed pass.

coreInvariants.name: Skip-reason encoding
coreInvariants.statement: UserMigrationSkipped.reason is empty <=> the migration was never attempted
coreInvariants.evidence: Empty reason is emitted at exactly two sites, both before any attempt: the dust-band skip (:198) and skipCurrent (:287). Non-empty reason is emitted only from the catch (:210), carrying raw ABI-encoded revert data from an attempted migrateOne. Matches the INVARIANT documented in IMigratorV2V3.sol:68-73. This is the story-028 delta.

coreInvariants.name: Reseed only between passes
coreInvariants.statement: seedUsers cannot replace the list mid-pass
coreInvariants.evidence: `require(!seeded || migrateIterator == -1, "Pass in progress")` at :145. First call passes on !seeded; later calls require a completed pass. Replaces the list wholesale (:148-151) and resets the cursor to 0 (:154).

coreInvariants.name: Reward-delta bracketing nets out the principal
coreInvariants.statement: phUSD delta across the withdraw+stake block equals the reward component only
coreInvariants.status: verified (cross-contract legs confirmed against PhlimboV2/PhlimboV3 source)
coreInvariants.evidence: Balances snapshotted at :243-246, deltas computed at :260-264 after phlimboV2.withdraw(:250) and phlimboV3.stake(:256). The principal is received then restaked so it nets out. Both cross-contract legs confirmed: (a) PhlimboV2.withdraw routes 100% of principal AND auto-claimed rewards to msg.sender — principal via PhlimboV2.sol:392, minted phUSD reward via _claimRewards(user, msg.sender) at PhlimboV2.sol:373 -> :495, stable reward via :500; `user` is only debited (:384-386) and never a payee. (b) PhlimboV3.stake pulls exactly `amount` from msg.sender (PhlimboV3.sol:661) and routes its own auto-claim to msg.sender (:657). So the bracketing is exact on both passes. RESIDUAL ASSUMPTION: no fee-on-transfer on any of the three tokens.
coreInvariants.dustRuleInteraction: PhlimboV2.withdraw carries a dust rule (PhlimboV2.sol:375-382) that can silently withdraw MORE than the requested `amount` when the residual would be non-zero but sub-MINIMUM_STAKE. It is INERT on the migrate path: migrate passes the full live `amount` read at :192, so remaining == 0 and the branch is not taken. MigratorV2V3's own dust-skip at :194-200 independently excludes sub-minStake positions.

invariantsNOTVerified.statement: unclaimable[token][user] is always backed by a real balance
invariantsNOTVerified.why: withdrawAll (:318-340) sweeps the ENTIRE phUSD/rewardToken/live-promo balances to the owner with NO reservation of `unclaimable` — unlike PhlimboV3.finalizePromotion which reserves totalUnclaimableOf. Documented as an accepted trade-off at :82-87 and IMigratorV2V3.sol:150-158: reimbursement becomes an out-of-band owner obligation. Note the deliberate asymmetry: MigratorV2V3 has NO `totalUnclaimable` counterpart to PhlimboV3's totalUnclaimableOf, precisely because it never needs to reserve. Recorded so downstream agents do not read this as an oversight.

invariantsNOTVerified.statement: The promo bracketing in migrateOne captures the full promo delta
invariantsNOTVerified.why: promoToken is read LIVE once at :241 and used for both the `before` snapshot (:245-246) and the `after` read (:262-264). If PhlimboV3's promo slot rotated mid-pass the two would still refer to the same token (cached in a local), so the delta is internally consistent. But whether the promo leg can be non-zero on a FIRST pass, and whether a rotation between migrate calls can strand promo tokens in this contract, is a cross-contract question. Deferred to interaction analysis.

localFindings.description: migrate is PERMISSIONLESS (no onlyOwner) — anyone may drive the pass at any chunk size, and each call issues `phUSD.forceApprove(address(phlimboV3), type(uint256).max)` (:178). Recipients and amounts are fixed by state (seeded list + live V2 reads), so a caller cannot redirect value. Surfaced for interaction analysis: the max-approve to PhlimboV3 is attacker-triggerable, though PhlimboV3.stake only pulls `amount` from msg.sender.
localFindings.recommendation: None at profile stage — for code-scanner to adjudicate.

localFindings.description: `uint256 end = i + maxIterations;` overflows and reverts for maxIterations near type(uint256).max, rather than clamping (clamp at :186 happens after the addition). Identical shape to PhlimboV3.batchClaim:455. Fails closed, no state written.

_tryTransfer is duplicated byte-for-byte across MigratorV2V3.sol:350-353 and PhlimboV3.sol:885-888 (verified by diff — see the divergence analysis below). Two independent copies of a security-relevant helper that must stay in lockstep; a future fix applied to one and not the other is a silent divergence. Same fork-drift class as the phoenix-nft-staking clone watch-note.
localFindings.recommendation: Extract to a shared library/base, or add a cross-file drift watch-note for future runs.

tryTransferDivergenceAnalysis.requested: Profile BOTH copies and note any divergence
tryTransferDivergenceAnalysis.method: sed -n '885,888p' src/PhlimboV3.sol vs sed -n '350,353p' src/MigratorV2V3.sol; diff returned empty
tryTransferDivergenceAnalysis.body: (bool callSuccess, bytes memory returndata) = address(token).call(abi.encodeCall(IERC20.transfer, (to, amount))); return callSuccess && (returndata.length == 0 || abi.decode(returndata, (bool)));
sharedSemantics: Returns true iff the low-level call succeeded AND (returndata is empty OR decodes to true) — the standard non-reverting SafeERC20-style acceptance rule.

NO code-existence check on `token`: a call to an address with NO CODE succeeds with empty returndata and is therefore treated as SUCCESS. In PhlimboV3.batchClaim the token is the owner-set, non-zero-checked promoToken (PhlimboV3.sol:356), so this is not reachable with address(0). In MigratorV2V3._forward the tokens are the immutable constructor-checked phUSD/rewardToken (:122-125) and the live promoToken, which is only forwarded under an explicit `address(promoToken) != address(0)` guard (:270-272). Recorded as a shared latent property of the helper, not adjudicated here.

abi.decode(returndata, (bool)) REVERTS (not returns false) if returndata is non-empty but shorter than 32 bytes or malformed. _tryTransfer is therefore NOT fully non-reverting against a non-conforming token — it is non-reverting against a token that cleanly reverts or cleanly returns false. Both copies share this property. Deferred to interaction analysis for exploitability.
tryTransferDivergenceAnalysis.callSiteDivergence: The helper bodies are identical, but the two call sites differ in what they do on failure — correctly, per their contracts: PhlimboV3.batchClaim banks into BOTH unclaimablePromoOf and totalUnclaimableOf (:479-480, the total being needed for the finalizePromotion sweep reservation), while MigratorV2V3._forward banks into `unclaimable` ONLY (:363), since withdrawAll deliberately reserves nothing (UNV-M-1). This is a designed asymmetry, not drift.

trustAssumptions: Deployment wiring is a PRECONDITION not enforced on-chain: phlimboV2.setMigrator(this) AND phlimboV3.setMigrator(this) (:48-52). A misconfigured pass still COMPLETES and marks migrateIterator = -1 — it merely emits a pass full of skips. The owner MUST read UserMigrationSkipped events after every pass before trusting it (:69-71). This is an explicit, documented operator obligation.
The seeded address list is produced by off-chain enumeration of V2 stakers — completeness of the list is not verifiable on-chain.
All three tokens are standard ERC20 with no fee-on-transfer (the balance-delta bracketing at :260-264 assumes exact transfers).
Owner is non-malicious (project Law 3); withdrawAll is an acknowledged unconditional escape hatch.
